title: LangSmith Self-Hosted
description: Operational dashboards for your own LangSmith deployment. Each component requires its documented telemetry collection. Filters select data, not access rights.

definition.content:
**Self-hosted SmithDB vitals.** Companion to the [SmithDB metrics reference](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-metrics). Scope with the **env**, **cluster**, and **namespace** variables.  
Metrics are queried under the `smithdb.` prefix. If your collector uses a different prefix, export this dashboard as JSON, replace `smithdb.` with your prefix, and import it. `langsmith_*` metrics are emitted by LangSmith and carry no prefix.

Green means healthy: query and ingest latency flat, pending counts steady, and all four error tiles at zero for the window. Pending compaction jobs and compaction failures are separate signals: jobs can fail while the queue stays flat, and the queue can grow while every job succeeds. [Baseline metrics](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-metrics#baseline-metrics)

Emitted by LangSmith, not SmithDB. End-to-end latency is the user-facing number; during dual ingestion compare `store:smithdb` against `store:clickhouse`. If **API to worker** rises, the LangSmith queue is the bottleneck, not SmithDB. If **Worker to store** rises, SmithDB writes are slow. [LangSmith ingestion path](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-metrics#langsmith-ingestion-path)

definition.title: Queue wait vs store write p95 (smithdb)

definition.content: Batch latency is received-to-flushed. Sustained growth in pending entries means flushing is backlogged. A flat flush rate while traffic arrives means writes are not landing. Rising flush duration points at object store latency or undersized ingestion. Permits in use pinned at max means writes are queuing. [Ingestion](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-metrics#ingestion)

definition.title: Flush trigger by reason and level
Concurrency permits in use vs max

definition.content: Status is the gRPC code; `0` is success. Rising fanout drives both latency and memory, and any sustained rejection rate means queries are failing outright. Peak operator memory approaching the configured limit precedes query termination. [Query](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-metrics#query)

definition.title: Scan fanout p95 by query type (top 8)

definition.content: Sustained growth in pending jobs means compaction is falling behind. A `job_kind` dropping to zero in completions means that job type has stopped running. Executed persistently below scheduled, or capacity used pinned at the limit, means workers are under-provisioned. Job latency includes queue wait, so it also rises when workers saturate. [Compaction](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-metrics#compaction)

Object store latency feeds every flush and compaction; split by op to separate reads from writes. Track resident memory against the pod memory limit. [All components](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/self-host-smithdb-metrics#all-components)

definition.title: Object store latency p95 by op

definition.content: Error-level logs from SmithDB services. Correlate a spike here with the failure tiles above to find which component is affected.

Import into your own Datadog organization and select one env, cluster and namespace for pool counts. Filters select data, not access rights. Fleet snapshots use 5m; other charts and totals follow the dashboard range. HTTP ranking uses whole-window p95. Legend AVG/MAX summarize plotted buckets. See the accompanying README for collection and optional integrations.

Snapshots use 5m; trends use the dashboard range. Per-host samples align for up to 60s. Ready/desired counts use max with interpolation off to avoid adding leader reports: select one cluster/namespace, not a multi-pool total. Missing data is unknown, not zero. Commitment is assigned capacity; desired replicas update only while scaling is active.

definition.title: Host pool: ready vs desired replicas

definition.content: Optional APM for public /v2/sandboxes routes. Internal reporting is separate. HTTP latency/rankings exclude streaming, tunnels and service proxy traffic. Only env and api_service filter APM; select exactly one API service. Metric/resource names can differ with instrumentation. 499 means a disconnected client.

Slowest public HTTP endpoints (window p95, ms)

definition.content: Compare API transport behavior with host-side command execution. API charts require APM; host command charts use the host scrape. WebSocket duration measures connection lifetime, not command runtime. Host and API filters apply to their respective sources.

definition.title: Exec HTTP: requests by status code
Exec WebSocket: requests by status code

Command runtime on host (mean ms) by class

definition.content: Error totals include operations without a recorded stage; the dedicated card keeps those failures visible. Stage rankings include outcome:error only. Non-ok outcomes also show cancellations/deadlines. Host duration charts show interval means, not percentiles.

definition.title: Operation error rate % by operation (outcome:error only)
Ref lock contention/s by operation (concurrent same-sandbox ops)
Ref lock wait (mean ms) by operation
Stage duration (mean ms) by stage — create
Stage duration (mean ms) by stage — start

definition.content: Distinguish warm-image restores from cold boots, then inspect provisioning stages and clone-slot waits. Zygote means a reusable warm VM image. Host boot readiness includes startup work, not just guest boot time.

definition.title: Zygote hit rate % (boots served from a warm image)
JuiceFS clone slot wait (mean ms) by clone type

definition.content: Short-request latency excludes WebSocket, SSE, tunnels and service proxy traffic. Their durations are shown separately in seconds; service proxy metrics mix ordinary HTTP and upgrades. VM lifetime ends on suspend/restart and is not the sandbox's total lifetime.

definition.title: Guest proxy requests/s by status class
No-target requests/s by route (sandbox moved or suspended)

definition.content: Guest resource totals across the selected hosts. CPU in use can exceed committed CPU during permitted bursts. Free-page-hint bytes and hint-round frequency use separate panels because they have different units.

definition.title: Guest CPU cores in use vs committed
Guest memory: resident vs returned to host

definition.content: Separate allowlist enforcement from proxy faults. access_denied is an expected policy denial and is excluded from the fault-rate percentage. DNS response codes can help explain guest network failures. Tenant rankings are intentionally omitted.

definition.title: Egress bytes/s by path and direction

definition.content: JuiceFS logical space/inodes require the mount's separate metrics scrape. Logical space includes apparent sparse and copy-on-write file sizes; no fixed ratio to physical bucket bytes applies. Host mount readiness uses the host scrape.

definition.title: JuiceFS logical used space (apparent, not stored)
JuiceFS metadata and cache (optional mount metrics)

definition.content: Optional mount metrics: metadata and Redis latency, retries, object-store performance, and cache behavior. Staging blocks and staging bytes are split so unlike units do not share an axis.

definition.title: Meta op latency (mean ms) by method

definition.content: Correlate failure counters with lease staleness, mount health, and logs. Empty counters can mean no events, missing collection, or a process exit before a scrape. Lease markers show four missed 15-second renewals and the current five-minute self-fence window.

Optional APM for internal /v2/sandboxes reporting and host-observation endpoints, excluded from public API traffic and latency. Select one API service. Only env and api_service filter these panels; host cluster/namespace filters do not apply.

definition.title: Internal reporting APM errors by endpoint

definition.content: Optional AWS/GCP integrations measure physical bucket storage, independently of host and APM filters. Select exact gcs_bucket and s3_bucket names; placeholder defaults match no buckets. Remove unused provider panels. Azure Blob Storage requires provider-specific queries.
